children: Carlsberg India Ltd, the Indian arm of Danish brewing giant Carlsberg, has moved a step closer to its stock market debut by filing updated draft papers with markets regulator SEBI for an initial public offering (IPO).

The proposed IPO is entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 8.64 crore equity shares by promoter South Asian Breweries Pvt Ltd, with no fresh issue component, according to the updated draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated October 27.
The development comes after the company received SEBI’s approval for its IPO on October 1, paving the way for further progress towards the public issue.
Carlsberg India had submitted its draft offer documents to SEBI through the confidential pre-filing route on July 1.
The confidential filing mechanism allows companies to submit draft offer documents to SEBI for review without immediately making commercially sensitive information public.

With this move, Carlsberg joins a growing list of multinational companies looking to tap India’s equity markets. South Korean conglomerates –Hyundai Motor and LG Electronics — have already listed their Indian subsidiaries.
Carlsberg India operates in the country with popular beer brands such as Tuborg, Carlsberg Elephant and Kronenbourg 1664 Blanc.
On the financial front, the company reported a 2.2% decline in revenue to ₹8,708.8 crore in FY26. However, its profit rose 22% to ₹534.51 crore during the fiscal year.
Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, Citigroup Global Markets India and JPMorgan India are the book-running lead managers to the public issue.

title: Carlsberg India moves closer to IPO: What its updated filing reveals about the beer maker
